title: Making Structs
story: You're building a contact list app. Your first friend profile worked great — now you need to add everyone else! One type, many profiles.
why: Once you define a struct type, you can create as many instances as you need — each one holds its own independent data.
analogy: A struct type is like a cookie cutter — one shape, but you can stamp out as many cookies as you want, each with different decorations.
try_it: Add a third person named "Taylor", age 13. Print all three names in a single sentence like "Alice, Bob, and Taylor are friends!"
tips: Each instance holds its own copy of every field — changing one does not affect another
You can create as many instances from one type as you need — no limit
If your variable name matches the field name, you can write `Person{ name, age }` instead of `Person{ name: name, age: age }`
common_mistakes: Reusing the same variable name and losing the first instance — use distinct variable names like `alice` and `bob`
Forgetting to print one person's data after focusing on the other — double-check both are displayed
